content.thinking:
I'm checking each claim against the source. The shoppers' account page outage duration and peak error rate both check out, and the monthly spending summary rollout is the trigger I'm still confirming for the next point.

I'm working through the remaining claims in turn: the cause line is only hedged support, and the customer-loss estimate and the missing page are both backed by the record. The feature-flag rollback is confirmed by the timeline entries, and the proposed fix is still an unreviewed draft that hasn't gone live.

content.text: I checked eight claims in the overview against the record and found none to flag.

supported.quote: Account pages on io-shop failed for shoppers for {duration}
rows: How long it lasted: at least 20m 55s {duration}

supported.quote: at the worst minute {peak_error_rate} of requests failed
rows: Requests failing at the worst minute: 37.0% {peak_error_rate}

supported.quote: The trouble began when a new monthly spending summary was switched on for account pages.
The summary likely divides by the number of things a shopper has bought this month, so it likely breaks for shoppers who have not bought anything yet this month.
rows: Why, in plain words: Switching on a new monthly spending summary

supported.quote: Argus estimates the incident cost the shop {customer_loss} in takings.
rows: What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): at least 8,253.46 USD {customer_loss}

supported.quote: No one was paged, and no on-call incident was linked to this one.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

supported.quote: Argus switched off the new summary's feature flag, but that did not help, so Argus switched it back on.
Argus has also proposed a fix, but it is still an unreviewed draft and has not been put into use.
